title: resolveTeam uses bidirectional substring matching that can over-match short names
evidence: src/queries.ts:26 `partial = [...all].filter(k => k.includes(key) || key.includes(k))` — a short query key (e.g. a team whose key is a substring of several canonical keys) resolves to multiple teams and silently aggregates them
suggestion: Prefer exact key match, then word-boundary/startsWith matching; only fall back to substring when no better match exists, and surface ambiguity

title: Performance specs assert on real wall-clock elapsed time
evidence: test/drivers/McpSoccerDriver.ts:68 assertElapsed + test/acceptance/soccer-knowledge.spec.ts:133-139 assert <2000ms/<5000ms; each spin-ups a fresh tsx MCP subprocess so timing is environment-dependent and can flake under load
suggestion: Keep a generous threshold or mark these as smoke/perf tests separate from the functional suite

title: A spec expectation was changed to match the dataset (Ederson as top Brazilian GK)
evidence: docs/atdd-findings.md:4 notes the spec assumed Alisson; test/acceptance/soccer-knowledge.spec.ts:85 now asserts confirmTopPlayerIs('Ederson')
suggestion: Defensible data-driven correction; documented in atdd-findings.md — no action needed, flagged for cross-run comparability

title: Several analytics tools provided beyond the required capabilities
evidence: src/server.ts registers derbies, biggest_wins, best_record, compare_seasons, top_scoring_teams in addition to the spec's required match/team/player/competition/stat queries
